items.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Concludes Without Iran Diplomatic Opening; Tariff Truce Extended; Boeing Purchases Announced; Post-Summit IRGC Cyber Window Now Open
items.summary: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit concluded today May 15 as Trump departed China, closing the inhibiting window that had marginally suppressed near-term IRGC retaliatory incentives since May 12. The summit's deliverables were consistent with pre-summit analyst consensus from CSIS, Chatham House, and CFR: a tariff truce extension (continuation of the October 2025 Busan framework) and Boeing aircraft purchase announcements. No joint statement committing Xi Jinping to engage Tehran directly on Hormuz reopening or nuclear concessions was released. The summit's Iran track outcome is structurally identical to the May 14 brief's assessment: the most hoped-for diplomatic catalyst — Xi as interlocutor between Washington and Tehran — did not materialize. Markets are reacting positively to the tariff truce headline (early gains noted by Schwab on 'retail sales, Cisco, China trip') but the tariff truce extension does not offset the Hormuz supply shock and generates no oil price relief. With Trump now departed from Beijing, the diplomatic inhibiting effect on resumed military action and IRGC cyber pre-positioning has expired. The post-summit period — May 15 onward — is the highest-priority IRGC cyber watch window of the current cycle. No Project Freedom resumption order has been issued as of this brief; any CENTCOM repositioning announcement, congressional notification, or Trump Truth Social signal in the next 24-72 hours is the highest-priority geopolitical watch item of the post-summit period.

items.headline: Israel-Hezbollah Ceasefire Expires May 17 — 48-Hour Clock; UAE Exited OPEC Effective May 1
items.summary: Two secondary geopolitical threads warrant elevation. First: the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire that was extended on April 23 for three additional weeks expires May 17 — 48 hours from today. The truce has remained fragile throughout its extension period, with Israel preserving the right to take defensive measures and Hezbollah continuing periodic drone and rocket targeting of Israeli troops and border communities. If the ceasefire collapses or is not renewed on May 17, the Iran war gains a second active front at precisely the moment the Trump-Xi summit has closed without producing a Hormuz off-ramp. A Lebanon escalation would raise Iranian incentives for direct military engagement and further complicate any residual diplomatic track. This is a 48-hour watch item with direct compound-risk implications for the primary Hormuz crisis. Second: the UAE's exit from OPEC, effective May 1, is now operative. The UAE departure reduces OPEC's institutional coherence and removes one of the Gulf states historically most engaged in production discipline negotiations. For oil price dynamics, the UAE exit raises questions about Abu Dhabi's independent production posture and whether OPEC+ can maintain coordinated output policy during the Hormuz disruption period. Neither development reverses the Hormuz supply shock; both introduce additional structural uncertainty.

items.headline: Warsh Day 1: April PPI +1.4% Monthly / Core +1.0% — 3x Consensus; Oil-Shock Inflation Accelerating on Fed Transition Day
items.summary: Kevin Warsh's first day as Federal Reserve Chair begins with the most adverse inaugural inflation data of any modern Fed chair transition. April producer price index data released today shows US wholesale prices rising 1.4% month-over-month — 3.5 times the 0.4% consensus estimate — with core PPI surging 1.0% against a 0.3% consensus, 3.3 times expectations. The April PPI print confirms what the May 14 brief characterized as structurally certain: the Hormuz supply shock (now at Day 76) is transmitting aggressively into upstream wholesale price inflation, and that transmission is accelerating, not plateauing. For Warsh, this data creates an immediate policy dilemma: the oil-shock PPI print argues against rate cuts (rate cuts in an oil-shock-inflation environment risk fueling price pressure), but Trump has publicly and repeatedly pressed for rate cuts, and Warsh's June 16-17 FOMC is now only 32 days away. The PPI print further reinforces the structural constraint flagged in yesterday's brief: the primary economic shock — Hormuz supply disruption — is immune to interest-rate tools, meaning the Fed cannot directly address the inflation driver regardless of its policy stance. Warsh's first public statement as chair — expected imminently — will be parsed intensely for any signal on inflation tolerance, rate-cut timeline, and independence posture. Jerome Powell, meanwhile, remains on the Board of Governors through his governor term expiring January 2028 despite his chair term ending today.

items.headline: VA Approves $596M Infrastructure; Gateway Hudson Tunnel Project Ready to Bore — $16B, Largest Modern US Transit Project; Chicago CTA Sues DOT/FTA for $2B
items.summary: Three significant infrastructure items away from the wildfire and cyber domains. The Department of Veterans Affairs approved $596 million in infrastructure improvements for FY2026 Q2, part of a record $4.8 billion in non-recurring maintenance funds VA will deploy this fiscal year across medical facilities for maintenance, replacements, and operational upgrades. The Hudson River Gateway Tunnel project — the largest modern US mass transit infrastructure project in generations at approximately $16 billion — is reaching the active boring phase: giant tunnel-boring machines nearly two football fields in length will begin chewing through dense rock connecting New Jersey and New York City, with crews managing conveyor systems hauling debris and installing curved concrete lining. The project represents the most significant Northeast rail corridor infrastructure investment in decades. Meanwhile, the Chicago Transit Authority has sued the Department of Transportation and FTA for withholding over $2 billion in funding tied to Red Line expansion and O'Hare International Airport modernization — the CTA's action joins a pattern of municipal and state infrastructure bodies challenging federal funding withholding that has emerged across the reconciliation and budget dispute period. In California, Project Nexus — a first-of-its-kind $20 million solar-covered irrigation canal in the Central Valley — is now operational, testing solar panel installation over canals for simultaneous clean energy generation and evaporation reduction.
